pack.title: Sibling digs
pack.description: Correct a dismissive joke without turning dinner into a debate.

scenarios.setting: Your sibling mocks your choice of career during a family meal.
scenarios.jab: Must be nice to get paid for playing on a laptop.
scenarios.goal: Correct a dismissive joke without turning dinner into a debate.

replies.line: It's my work. I'd like you to speak about it respectfully.
replies.why: It corrects the framing and states the behavior you want.
replies.delivery: Keep “my work” calm; if the joke repeats, change seats or end the topic.

replies.line: It's work. Drop the dig, please.
replies.why: It gives a direct boundary without returning a personal insult.
replies.delivery: Say “It's work” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Change seats or end the topic.

replies.line: I enjoy what I do; that joke makes it sound like it doesn't count.
replies.why: It explains the impact without attacking your sibling's job.
replies.delivery: Keep “I enjoy what I do” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Change seats or end the topic.

replies.line: My laptop and the tax office both call it work.
replies.why: A joke adds perspective without suggesting your sibling is less successful.
replies.delivery: Keep “My laptop and the tax office both call” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Change seats or end the topic.

followUp.line: I can enjoy a joke; I'm asking you to leave my work out of it.
followUp.why: It distinguishes humor from a repeated target you do not welcome.
followUp.delivery: Keep “my work” calm; if the joke repeats, change seats or end the topic.
